content:
I just discovered a feature hidden in the System Settings app that I never knew existed: you can set a default language for individual Mac apps. If you already knew about this, there's nothing to see here, move along. But if not, here's how it works (or doesn't)…

A lot of bilingual people have to switch languages throughout the day depending on who they're talking to and what they're doing. I don't really have that problem, but I do find myself often switching between British English (and English…) and American English.

(Just to be clear, that was a joke! There are elements of English that are retained in American English but changed later in British English, such as -ize endings becoming -ise in the UK. And, as James Nicoll said: "The problem with defending the purity of the English language is that English is roughly the size of a prostitute in a brothel. We don't just borrow words; on occasion, English has chased other languages down alleyways to beat them unconscious and rifle through their pockets for new vocabulary.")

Switching between the two means I can't rely on spell check to catch cases where I've used the right word but the wrong language version. I always assumed this was something I just had to handle manually, but today I found out there's at least a partial solution.

Hidden at the bottom of "System Settings > General > Language & Region" is an "Applications" section. You can add apps here and pick a language. Apple's American-centrism is on full display here—British English is called "English (UK)", while American English is called "English – English".

In my case, since most of my writing happens in a browser, I use two different browsers depending on the target language. I have British English set as my system language, so Safari uses British English, and Chrome (which appears alphabetically in the list as Google Chrome) is set to American English.

As I discovered, there's an important caveat here: only apps that support macOS's localization/language API can be configured this way, so not every app will show up in the list.

If I'm the last person on Earth to find out about this, feel free to cast your linguistically superior shade in the comments.
